titleStmt.title: Memorandum From the Executive Secretary of the Department of State (Bremer) to the President’s Assistant for National Security Affairs (Allen)

div.head: 460. Memorandum From the Executive Secretary of the Department of State (Bremer) to the President’s Assistant for National Security Affairs (Allen)
div.p: Venezuelan President Luis Herrera Campins has been advised of President Reagan’s invitation to visit Washington April 13. The Venezuelans are delaying their acceptance until we can clarify what the visit will involve. We strongly recommend that it be a state visit, or at least one that is comparable in style.

Venezuela is one of the three countries in Latin America most important to the United States, not only because of its petroleum but also because of its active and positive political role in Central America and the Caribbean. Venezuela pursues foreign policy goals in the hemisphere which generally coincide with ours, seeking to compete effectively with Cuba in the Caribbean area and strongly supporting the government of El Salvador.

Previous Venezuelan President Carlos Andres Perez made a state visit in June 1977. Any significant disparity between the treatment accorded President Herrera and his predecessor, who is from the opposition party, would be widely commented on, and damaging politically, in the lively competition between the two major parties of Venezuela’s vigorous democracy.

President Herrera is Venezuela’s Chief of State. We believe we can design a state visit along the lines of the attached illustrative schedule which would take little more of President Reagan’s time than a working visit, yet would indicate to the Venezuelans and all Latin Americans the importance this Administration attaches to our relationship with Venezuela, with consequent benefits to our relations.

Venezuelan Ambassador Perez Chiriboga planned to go to Caracas on March 24 to consult with his government on acceptance of the invitation and planning for the visit. He is delaying his trip until we are able to be specific on the outlines for the schedule. We would therefore appreciate a response as soon as possible.

note.p: Source: Reagan Library, Executive Secretariat, NSC Country File, Latin America/Central, Venezuela (02/28/1981–04/03/1981). Confidential. Fontaine sent the memorandum to Allen under cover of a March 25 memorandum in which he noted that arguments for a full State visit “are cogent and convincing,” adding: “But the matter has already been decided. There will be full State visit for President Herrera.”

In telegram 72867 to Caracas, March 21, the Department instructed the Embassy to invite Herrera on Reagan’s behalf to visit Washington on April 13. (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D810135–0150) In telegram 2965 from Caracas, March 23, Luers reported that he had conveyed the invitation to Foreign Minister Zambrano who asked for details about the proposed visit. (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D810135–1102)
See Foreign Relations, 1977–1980, vol. XXIV, South America; Latin America Region, Document 336.
Attached but not printed is an illustrative schedule.
Kelly signed for Bremer above Bremer’s typed signature.
